title: Always in need of renewal
hookLine: Vatican II says Christ calls the Church to continual reformation (Unitatis Redintegratio 6)

cards: Scaffolding climbs one tower of an old cathedral while Mass goes on inside. Stonemasons up top replace what the weather wore away; a choir below sings what it has sung for generations.

The scaffolding doesn't mean the building is false. It means the building is still in use. At the Second Vatican Council, the bishops wrote a sentence about the Church that sounds like that scaffolding.
It's in a document on Christian unity, and it says the Church is always being called to renewal.

teach.b: In paraphrase, the sentence says this: Christ calls the Church, still on her journey, to keep reforming, and she always needs it, because she is also a human institution on earth. Take it a piece at a time.
First, who calls. The council doesn't say reform is a good idea people had. It says the call comes from Christ.

The passage names failings in conduct, in church discipline, even in the way teaching has been worded, and says these should be set right, while keeping distinct the faith itself, which it does not treat as up for change.

Third, the road of these past weeks held both. A wounded soldier praying in Manresa, Teresa on the road, Vincent de Paul and the poor, Kongo's king, Mother Seton's schools, the hidden families of Japan.
And Galileo, the slave trade, the pain of the California missions, the Jesuits suppressed.

teach.h: RENEWAL AND FAILURE, SIDE BY SIDE.
teach.b: Renewal and failure, side by side, in the same Church. Fourth, the person.
Catholic teaching speaks of conversion not as something done once, but as a lifelong task for every baptized person. What is true of the Church is true of each member.

teach.h: BEHOLD, I MAKE ALL THINGS NEW.
teach.b: In the Apocalypse, also called Revelation, in the Douay-Rheims, the one on the throne says: "Behold, I make all things new." Not once and finished. Being made new.

how: Catholics speak of continual conversion, renewed through confession, Lent and retreats, and parishes and dioceses hold synods and renewal programs to examine how they live the faith.

o: the continual reform the Church always needs
a council's one-time reform of the Mass

games.q: always in need of renewal — tap the pairs.
p: comes from Christ, the council says
what the passage says may need setting right
a lifelong task, not a single moment

s: the Second Vatican Council said the Church never needs reform
it says Christ calls the Church to keep reforming, which she always needs because she is also a human institution.
the council treats renewal as throwing out the faith itself
it names failings in conduct, discipline and wording, and keeps the faith itself distinct.
Catholic teaching describes conversion as a lifelong task
what is true of the Church is true of each member.

games.q: you're one of the bishops at the council, writing about the Church. do you say she needs reform?
o: no. say the Church has never needed fixing.
yes. say Christ calls her to continual reformation.
games.why: the council wrote, in effect, that Christ calls the Church on her journey to keep reforming, which she always needs because she is also a human institution.

practice: Think of one habit, one relationship, one corner of your life that has worn down, the way stone wears in weather; not everything, just one.

Don't tear it down in your head; ask what a small repair would look like: an apology, a return to something you dropped, a kinder way of speaking. If you pray, ask God for help with it; if you don't, simply hold it honestly.

wordCard.voice: Perennis reformatio. Latin for continual reformation, the council's phrase for how Christ keeps calling the Church, and every member of it, to be made new.

orig.note: Latin: continual reformation, the council's phrase (as perennem reformationem) in Unitatis Redintegratio 6.

carryVoice: Your line: always renewing. Tomorrow, the modern Church begins, with a struggling parish priest in a French village. That's day eight hundred eighty-six.

sources.q: Behold, I make all things new.
